$comment: Run of show for the LED wall behind the main stage. Talk titles, names and portraits come from content/2026-announcements.json by slug; this file adds only what the wall needs on top: job titles, the day, and the order of cues. Edit it, then run `node stage/build.mjs` (stage/render.mjs does that for you). Times and the order of the `days` cues follow the final schedule in content/2026-schedule.json (node stage/sync-schedule.mjs); `breakout` per day is the breakout screen's own run of show.

wall.$comment: 3696×1176 confirmed by the AV vendor. The cabinet size is ASSUMED: both sides divide by 168, so 22 × 7 cabinets of 168×168 px. Every layout is positioned against this canvas.

music.$comment: Music by scene. `sets` are playlists that crossfade track to track and loop; `scenes` picks a set per scene, and a cue's own `music` (a set name, or false) overrides it. `walkon` is a list of short themes; each walk-on plays the next one in turn, so consecutive talks never repeat, over a quick fade of whatever was playing. Nothing plays during a talk. In most venues this goes to the sound desk rather than out of the wall laptop — agree with the AV vendor which.
music.$announce: Each walk-on's announcement starts `delay` seconds into the theme; the theme drops to `duck` of its volume under the voice and comes back after it.

$ticker: Walk-in and break scenes have no sponsor row by default: the sponsor wall is part of their loop instead. A cue's `ticker` (a list of tiers, e.g. ["Platinum", "Gold"]) brings the row back: six white hexagons across the bottom, the logos changing in groups every 7 s.

announce.$comment: The voice of god on every main-stage walk-on: the hosts' and each speaker's. The control page has three modes on the main stage: All sessions (the default), Hosts only (just the hosts' welcome, wrap-ups and remarks, so the hosts introduce every speaker themselves) and Off; v steps through them. The breakout has Off (its default) and All sessions. The walk-on theme plays in every mode. ElevenLabs voice "Brian" (nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb), eleven_multilingual_v2, stability 0.4, style 0.45, speed 0.92; trimmed and normalised to -15 LUFS into assets/audio/announce/<slug>.mp3. The build picks a clip up by slug. These are the words as sent, names spelled for the voice. Any talk can have one: add its words here and a clip at that path.

talks.$comment: Stage items that are not in content/2026-announcements.json: remarks, the charity partner, wrap-ups. Same shape the build produces for announcement talks. `kind` is the eyebrow.

qr.$comment: QR codes on the wall and the breakout screen are drawn from content/2026-qr.json, which stage/import-qr.py reads out of QR PNGs. The feedback codes are Sessionize's export (organizer dashboard → Session Feedback → download QR codes), keyed by session id; the feedback scene shows the one for the talk the room just had. `photos` is the photographers' Picdrop gallery, in the break loops; the build encodes the link itself (stage/qr.mjs). The build encodes every link here the same way into SHOW.qrs, for the decks: `aalborg`, `aarhus` and `copenhagen` are the meetup groups on the local communities slide.

social.$comment: The `social` scene, in the pre-show and countdown loops. The prize line matches the decks.
social.prize: Three best posts win, drawn on day two.

$walkonSeconds: A talk goes live by itself this long after its walk-on, in time with the sting. Next still goes live straight away; set 0 to always wait for Next.
$clearBeforeWalkon: Every talk starts on a clear wall: the faint field only, no text, no music. The next press brings the walk-on and its music. So a talk is three presses: clear, walk-on, live (live also comes by itself after walkonSeconds).
$countdown: A countdown cue starts at `minutes` (default 5) the moment it comes up on the wall, and counts down. The control page can restart or nudge it. `at` is only the fallback for renders.
$loop: A cue's `loop` alternates between these scenes (hexagon wave between them) while its music carries on. `every` is the seconds per scene: one number for all, or a list with one per scene ([40, 10, 10]: 40 s countdown, 10 s sponsors, 10 s hashtags, every minute). `holdLast` keeps a countdown on its first scene for its final seconds. The phase comes from the clock, so the wall and the control preview switch together.
